No. 650. 1377. 27. Jimi. K. Karl IV. bedroht auf Grund eingegangener Beschwerde Fiirsten, Grafcn, Herren und Stddte der Magdeburger Kirchenprovinz, welche die Geistlichkeit in ihrcn Giitem, Erwerbungen, Rechten und Freiheiten beeintrdchtigen und schddigen, mit namhafter Strafe und erkldrt alle in diesem Sinne bestehenden Einrichtungen und Vorschriften fiir nichtig.

In nom. s. et ind. tr. feliciter amen. Karolus quartus divina favente clementia Romanorum imperator semper augustus et Bohemiae rex ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Etsi imperialis benignitatis clementia quorumlibet devotorum fidelium, quos sacrum Romanum ambit imperium ex officii debito teneatur necessitatibus et iniustis oppres- sionibus consulere et de oportunis remediis providere, ad illos tamen permaxime diri- gitur nostrae mentis affectio, quos indebite pati cognoscimus, quorumque oppressio- nibus status ecclesiasticae libertatis, quem semper nostris temporibus augeri volumus, nonnihilum minuitur et minus debite praegravatur. Sane ad imperialis maiestatis audientiam pro parte honorabilium praepositi, decani et aliorum praelatorum, canoni- corum et capituli Magdeburgensis ecclesiae, devotorum nostrorum dilectorum insinua- tione querulosa suppliciter est deductum, quod saeculares quidam in potestatibus et officiis publicis constituti videlicet duces comites barones et alii domini temporales, nec non consules civitatum opidorum villarum et locorum rectores dictae Magdebur- gensis provinciae, dei timore postposito statuta singularia et iniquas ordinationes motu proprio et de facto contra personas ecclesiasticas, ecclesiarum libertates et privilegia condiderunt, eisque publice et de facto insistere praesumpserunt contra legitimas civiles et canonicas sanctiones, ut puta quod nulla bona temporalia in potestatem ecclesiasticam transferantur, neve clerici in sacris constituti ad agendum et testifi- candum in civilibus et maxime in piis causis aliquatenus admittantur, quodque excommunicati laici et publice denunciati in civili foro minime repellantur. Item praedicti domini temporales consules et rectores per secularem potestatem res et bona clericorum occupant et arrestant, oblationes fidelium diminuunt et restringunt, exactio- nes et tallias indebitas de bonis et redditibus ecclesiae exigunt et extorquent, posses- siones ecclesiae et personarum eorumdem devastant incendiis et rapinis, contractus inter clericos et laicos factos legittime ad libros civitatum, villarum et locorum recu- sant inscribere et sigillare, donata et legata ad fabricas et ecclesiarum structuras contra praelatorum voluntatem et aliorum quorum interest, praesumunt usurpare contra iustitiam in fraudem et odium clericorum, de bonis etiam et rebus clericorum quas non causa negotiationis, sed pro usibus propriis per terras ducunt seu duci faciunt, theloneum exigere et recipere non verentur, et confugientes ad ecclesias et cimiteria inde extrahere contra sanctiones imperiales praesumunt. Quae omnia et quaelibet obinde secuta, cum per sacras, civiles et canonicas sanctiones expresse reprobata ,sunt et in fraudem ecclesiasticae libertatis de facto praesumpta, de princi- pum ducum comitum baronum fideliumque nostrorum consilio ex certa scientia aucto- ritate imperiali cassamus, irritamus et annullamus, cassaque irrita et nullius esse momenti penitus dicimus et expresse pronunciamus, praecipientes sub indignatione 168 imperialis banni universis et singulis dictae Magdeburgensis provinciae et locorum vicinorum principibus et dominis temporalibus consulibus potestatibus et in officiis publicis constitutis, quatenus mox visis aut intellectis praesentibus dicta ipsorum sta- tuta et ordinationes, sicut in praeiudicium ecclesiasticae Hbertatis edita sunt, omnino revocent et de luce tollant, quodque secundum ea non iudicent amplius nec senten- tias dictent, aut eisdem in iudicio vel extra iudicium quomodolibet per se et contra ecclesiasticam libertatem potiantur. Item pronunciamus et declaramus imperiali auto- ritate, quod quicunque laicus, cuiuscumque status vel conditionis extiterit, ausu sacri- lego et propriae temeritatis audacia sacerdotem vel clericum secularem vel religiosum diffidaverit proscripserit captivaverit spoliaverit occiderit mutilaverit aut in carcere detinuerit, ac huiusmodi maleficia perpetrantes scienter receptaverit vel favorem in his eis praestiterit, praeter poenas a sacris imperialibus et canonicis sanctionibus eis inflictas, sint ipso facto infames et omni honore privati, nec ad placita vel consilia nobilium admittendi quovismodo. Volumus etiam hortamur et requirimus episcopos et praelatos ecclesiasticos, ut hanc nostram legem et constitutionem in synodis et ecclesiis publicari procurent, ne in praemissis excedentes per simulatam ignorantiam suas malicias valeant excusare. Nulli ergo omnino hominum liceat hanc nostrae cassationis irritationis annullationis seu pronunciationis et declarationis paginam ausu temerario infringere aut ei quomodolibet contraire sub poena quinquaginta marcharum auri puri, quas ab eo, qui contrafecerit tocies, quocies contra factum fuerit, irremissi- biliter exigi volumus et earum medietatem nostri imperialis aerarii, residuam vero partem iniuriam passorum usibus decernimus applicari. Signum sere - (Monogramm) nissimi principis et domini domini Karoli quarti Romanorum imperatoris invictissimi et gloriosissimi Bohemiae regis. Testes huius rei sunt venerabiles Johannes Pra- gensis archiepiscopus, apostolicae sedis legatus, Heinricus Warmiensis episcopus, illustres Sigismundus Brandemburgensis marchio sacri imperii archicamerarius princeps elector, Johannes Gorlicensis et Heinricus Rassiensis duces, spectabiles Burghardus burkgrauius Magdeburgensis et comes in Hardek, Mathias comes de Brebetio, nobiles Petrus de Wartemberg imperialis curiae nostrae magister et Heinricus de Rosemberg, neenon alii quam plures nostri et imperii sacri principes, nobiles et fideles, praesen- tium sub imperiali nostrae maiestatis sigillo testimonio litterarum. Datum Tanger- munde anno domini millesimo trecentesimo septuagesimo septimo indictione quinta decima V. Kalend. Julii, regnorum nostrorum anno tricesimo primo, imperii vero vicesimo tertio. Nach dem Orig. im Provinzialarchiv zu Magdeburg. Das kaiserl. Majestatssiegel mit Rticksiegel hangt an gelbseidenen Faden. Im Stiftsarchiv zu Meissen befindet sich ein iu mehreren Stellen ungenaues und fehler- haftes Transsumt v. J. 1395. 169
entries.english:
No. 650. 27 June 1377. Emperor Karl IV, following a complaint, threatens substantial penalties against the princes, counts, lords and towns of the ecclesiastical province of Magdeburg who impair or injure the clergy in their property, acquisitions, rights and liberties, and declares all existing measures and regulations to that effect void.

In the name of the holy and indivisible Trinity, amen. Karl IV, by the favor of divine clemency Roman emperor, ever august, and king of Bohemia, for the perpetual remembrance of the matter. Although imperial clemency is bound by the duty of its office to attend to the needs and unjust oppression of all devoted subjects embraced by the Holy Roman Empire and to provide suitable remedies, our concern is directed above all to those whom we know to suffer unjustly and whose oppression diminishes and unduly burdens the state of ecclesiastical liberty, which we always wish to see increased in our times.

A complaint has humbly been brought to the attention of the imperial majesty on behalf of the honorable provost, dean, other prelates, canons and chapter of the church of Magdeburg, our beloved and devoted subjects. Certain laymen holding public powers and offices, namely dukes, counts, barons and other temporal lords, as well as councillors of cities, towns and villages and rulers of places in the said province of Magdeburg, have set aside the fear of God and, on their own initiative and in fact, made particular statutes and unjust ordinances against ecclesiastical persons and the liberties and privileges of churches. They have presumed to enforce them openly and in fact, contrary to lawful civil and canon law: for example, that no temporal goods be transferred into ecclesiastical hands; that clerics in holy orders be in no way admitted to bring actions or give testimony in civil cases, especially those concerning pious causes; and that excommunicated laymen who have been publicly denounced be by no means excluded from the civil court.

Furthermore, the aforesaid temporal lords, councillors and rulers, by secular power, seize and place under restraint the property and goods of clerics; diminish and restrict the offerings of the faithful; demand and extort improper exactions and taxes from the goods and revenues of the Church; devastate the possessions of the Church and of those persons by fire and plunder; refuse to enter in the registers of cities, towns and places and to seal contracts lawfully made between clerics and laymen; and presume unjustly to appropriate gifts and legacies for the building and fabric of churches against the wishes of the prelates and others concerned, to the detriment of and out of hatred for the clergy. They also do not hesitate to demand and receive tolls on clerics' goods and possessions which they transport or have transported through the lands for their own use, not for trade; and they presume, contrary to imperial laws, to remove from churches and churchyards those who have taken refuge there.

Since all these things and each consequence arising from them are expressly condemned by sacred, civil and canon law and have been presumptuously undertaken in violation of ecclesiastical liberty, we, on the counsel of the princes, dukes, counts, barons and our faithful subjects, knowingly and by imperial authority revoke, invalidate and annul them. We declare and expressly pronounce them utterly void, invalid and of no effect. Under threat of the imperial ban, we command each and every prince, temporal lord, councillor, holder of authority and public official of the said province of Magdeburg and neighboring places, as soon as they have seen or learned of these presents, entirely to revoke and abolish their said statutes and ordinances, since they were issued to the prejudice of ecclesiastical liberty; and thereafter neither to judge nor pronounce sentences according to them, nor in any way to use them in or out of court on their own authority against ecclesiastical liberty.

We further pronounce and declare by imperial authority that any layman, whatever his status or condition, who with sacrilegious daring and reckless audacity declares a feud against, proscribes, captures, robs, kills, mutilates or imprisons a priest or cleric, secular or religious, or knowingly shelters the perpetrators of such crimes or assists them in these acts, shall, in addition to the penalties imposed on them by sacred imperial and canon law, be infamous and deprived of every honor by that very act, and shall in no way be admitted to the assemblies or councils of nobles.

We also desire, exhort and require bishops and ecclesiastical prelates to have this law and constitution of ours published in synods and churches, so that those who transgress in these matters cannot excuse their wrongdoing by feigned ignorance. Let no one therefore dare rashly to infringe this document of our revocation, invalidation, annulment, pronouncement and declaration, or in any way contravene it, on pain of fifty marks of pure gold. We will that this sum be exacted without remission from the offender each time an offense is committed, and decree that half be applied to our imperial treasury and the remainder to the use of those who have suffered the injury.

The sign of the most serene prince and lord, Karl IV, the most invincible Roman emperor and most glorious king of Bohemia. [Monogram.] Witnesses to this matter are the venerable Hans, Erzbischof zu Prag, legate of the Apostolic See; Heinrich, Bischof zu Ermland; the illustrious Siegmund, Marggraf zu Brandenburg, archchamberlain of the Holy Empire and prince elector; Hans, Herzog zu Görlitz, and Heinrich, Herzog, styled Rassiensis; the distinguished Burghard, Burggraf zu Magdeburg and Graf zu Hardek; Mathias, Graf de Brebetio; the noble Peter de Wartemberg, master of our imperial court, and Heinrich von Rosenberg; and very many other princes, nobles and faithful subjects of ours and of the Holy Empire. In testimony of this, these letters are issued under the seal of our imperial majesty.

Given at Tangermünde in the year of the Lord 1377, in the fifteenth indiction, on the fifth day before the Kalends of July, in the thirty-first year of our reigns and the twenty-third of our empire.

From the original in the provincial archive at Magdeburg. The imperial seal of majesty with its counterseal hangs from yellow silk threads. The chapter archive at Meissen contains a 1395 transsumpt that is inaccurate and faulty in several places.
